# Chef cookbooks

<!-- Generated by tools/clientrecipes from src/chef.json; edit the source. -->

Read the [common setup and credential rules](README.md) first. [All recipes](index.md).

Client: **Chef 19.4.46, Knife 19.0.134, knife-art 1.0.2 (Ruby 4.0.9)**. Registered classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**.

Endpoint: `${AW_URL}/artifactory/api/chef/${AW_REPO}`

## Before connecting

- Install knife-art as well as knife; the plain knife supermarket client is not the authenticated integration exercised here.
- Export AW_REPO and AW_USER as well as AW_TOKEN.
- Python 3 is used only to URL-encode runtime credentials.

Authentication: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.

Fresh client state: Create a new AW_WORK with mktemp -d for every run; client configuration, downloads and caches in the commands stay under this directory. Do not reuse it to prove a fresh download. Remove the temporary directory after use.

## Configure

Save the Ruby configuration in the temporary directory. It resolves credentials from environment at invocation; only the runtime URL contains the token.

```sh
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
AW_AUTH_URL=$(python3 - <<'PYCODE'
import os
from urllib.parse import quote, urlsplit, urlunsplit
u = urlsplit(os.environ["AW_URL"])
auth = quote(os.environ["AW_USER"], safe="") + ":" + quote(os.environ["AW_TOKEN"], safe="")
print(urlunsplit((u.scheme, auth + "@" + u.netloc, u.path, "", "")))
PYCODE
)
export AW_AUTH_URL AW_WORK
cat > "$AW_WORK/chef.rb" <<'RUBY'
knife[:supermarket_site] = ENV.fetch("AW_AUTH_URL") + "/artifactory/api/chef/" + ENV.fetch("AW_REPO")
cookbook_path [File.expand_path("cookbooks", Dir.pwd)]
node_name ENV.fetch("AW_USER")
RUBY
```

## Publish

Classes: **local, federated**. Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

cookbooks/widget must contain metadata.rb and recipes; publish dependencies before the dependent cookbook.

```sh
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" CHEF_LICENSE=accept-no-persist knife artifactory share widget Other --config "$AW_WORK/chef.rb"
```

## Install or resolve

Classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**. Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

knife-art installation requires an initialized cookbook Git repository. Set a repository-local identity because the installer creates subsequent commits and tags; the isolated home has no global Git identity.

```sh
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/installed"
git -C "$AW_WORK/installed" init -b master
git -C "$AW_WORK/installed" config user.name "Recipe user"
git -C "$AW_WORK/installed" config user.email "recipe@example.invalid"
git -C "$AW_WORK/installed" commit --allow-empty -m initial
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" CHEF_LICENSE=accept-no-persist knife artifactory install widget 1.0.0 --cookbook-path "$AW_WORK/installed" --config "$AW_WORK/chef.rb"
```

## Limits

Classes outside **local, remote, virtual, federated** are not registered for this format. Commands above apply only to each operation's listed classes. Federated evidence is for one node; it does not establish cross-vendor replication.

- Federation is tested on one node. Chef server node-management APIs are outside this cookbook recipe.
